response: Resection of colorectal liver metastases (CLM) after second-line chemotherapy can be worthwhile. According to the available data, CLM resection following second-line chemotherapy, after oncosurgically favorable selection, could bring similar overall survival (OS) rates compared to what is observed after first-line chemotherapy. Additionally, for initially unresectable patients, overall survival (OS) or disease-free survival (DFS) is comparable between first- and second-line chemotherapy. Therefore, surgery should not be denied after the failure of first-line chemotherapy, and resection of CLM after second-line chemotherapy can be a viable treatment option.
